paths.name: react-toastify
paths.message: Import from "react-toastify/unstyled" instead. The two entry points are separate modules with separate state, so a `toast` from one never reaches a `ToastContainer` from the other - the toast simply never appears, and nothing fails. `/unstyled` also avoids injecting a <style> tag, which is why src/pages/_app.tsx imports the CSS instead.

no-restricted-syntax.message: dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders its input as raw HTML, and the app's only defence against stored XSS is that no raw-HTML sink exists. Every free-text column a user controls - user.bio, user.preferredName, user.pronouns, message.content, carpool_search.company_name, carpool_search.group_notes - is validated for length and nothing else (src/utils/textLimits.ts), so `<script>alert(1)</script>` is a legal value. Render it as JSX text and let React escape it. If the HTML is genuinely trusted and no part of it derives from user input, put `// eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-syntax` on the line above with a comment naming where the HTML comes from and why it is trusted.

dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders its input as raw HTML, and passing it through a props object rather than a JSX attribute changes nothing. See the JSX-attribute message above: render user-controlled text as JSX text and let React escape it. If the HTML is genuinely trusted, put `// eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-syntax` on the line above with a comment naming its source and why it is trusted.

.innerHTML and .outerHTML treat their value as markup: assigning to either parses the string as HTML and executes any script it contains, so a stored value carrying markup runs in the viewer's browser. Reading them is flagged too, because string-level DOM manipulation is how a value ends up being assigned back. Use .textContent for text, or build nodes with document.createElement. Mapbox popups must stay on .setText() rather than .setHTML() - src/utils/map/viewRoute.ts is the precedent. If raw HTML is genuinely required and its source is trusted, put `// eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-syntax` on the line above with a comment justifying the source.

insertAdjacentHTML parses its second argument as HTML, so any user-controlled value reaching it becomes stored XSS. Insert a text node, or build nodes with document.createElement. If raw HTML is genuinely required and its source is trusted, put `// eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-syntax` on the line above with a comment justifying the source.

document.write parses its argument as HTML into the document and executes any script in it. There is no reason to reach for it in a React application - render the content as JSX instead. If it is genuinely required and its input is trusted, put `// eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-syntax` on the line above with a comment justifying the source.
